title.en: Non-Cooperation, Swarajists and the Simon Commission

text.en: Across India in 1921 great heaps of foreign cloth burned in the streets, lawyers walked out of courts and children left government schools. Then a mob at Chauri Chaura turned violent, and Gandhi stopped everything.

The Congress approved non-cooperation at a special Calcutta session in September 1920 and at Nagpur in December 1920, chaired by Salem C. Vijayaraghavachariar.
It asked people to surrender titles, boycott schools, courts, councils and foreign goods, and spread Swadeshi.
Students left schools, lawyers gave up practice, and the Prince of Wales' visit was boycotted successfully.
On 5 February 1922 a procession at Chauri Chaura, near Gorakhpur, turned violent and 22 policemen died when the police station was burnt.
Gandhi immediately withdrew the movement because he held that only a non-violent struggle could succeed.
Congress split into pro-changers, who wanted to enter the legislatures, and no-changers like Vallabhbhai Patel and Rajaji, who wanted to continue non-cooperation.
C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru founded the Swaraj Party on 1 January 1923 and won many seats in the Legislative Councils.
Dyarchy under the 1919 Act divided provincial subjects into Reserved and Transferred, and it ended with provincial autonomy in 1935.
After Chauri Chaura Gandhi's constructive programme promoted khadi, Hindu-Muslim unity and the abolition of untouchability, and the All India Spinners' Association was formed.
On 8 November 1927 the British appointed the all-white Indian Statutory Commission under Sir John Simon, and everywhere crowds cried Go Back Simon.
Lala Lajpat Rai was injured by a police assault in Lahore and died a few days later.
An all-party conference in 1928 appointed a committee under Motilal Nehru, whose Nehru Report asked for Dominion status, joint electorates and fundamental rights.
Jinnah's amendments, called his Fourteen Points, were rejected, and he later began to espouse a separate nation for Muslims.

problem.en: Why did Gandhi withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement?

text.en: On 5 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura a mob burnt a police station.
So he called it off, though many leaders were disappointed.

why.en: This led to the Swarajist split.

prompt.en: State the main points of the Nehru Report.

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the Simon Commission wrote it

points.en: Simon Commission was all-white, so it was boycotted.
